You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

The rule generalizes to 30x30 -> 10x10 as well as the smaller grids noted above.", path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T10:20:56.555363+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T11:59:24.245639+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_7064b436_fill_gaps_in_broken_rectangle_border_with_2', kind='memory', title='ARC task-7064b436: fill gaps in broken rectangle border with 2', content='For task-7064b436, the grid has a large axis-aligned rectangular outline in a foreground color (demo: 3 on background 6; test: 5 on 7), with missing cells along its four sides. Added after validating demos: other examples show a border can be complete while an internal repeated-marker line still needs bridging.', path='arc-patterns', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={'task_id': 'task-7064b436'}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T11:05:43.708478+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T11:58:39.279042+00:00', version=7), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_b0146853_move_object_against_divider_and_add_8_line', kind='memory', title='ARC task-b0146853: move object against divider and add 8-line', content='For ARC task-b0146853: Grid has uniform background, a full horizontal or vertical divider line (color 2 in demos), and a non-background object on one side. Move/translate the entire object toward the divider until its nearest bounding edge is immediately adjacent to it (preserve object shape and color; do not leave its original copy). Paint full column c4 color 8 (the line immediately beyond the translated shape, opposite the divider); leave all other cells unchanged. Accepted after one incorrect answer. Important parsing lesson: the last singleton was at row 14, not row 15; preserve exact shape rows while translating.

More demos: (a) vertical divider c2, object touching it at c3-4; add full color-8 column c5, do not move the object. (b) vertical divider c3, singleton left of it at c2; add full color-8 column c1.
